datasets.title: Satellite-detected flood waters over Mobayi-Mbongo, Nord-Ubangi Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20191118COD This map illustrates satellite-detected flooded waters along the Ubangui River over Mobayi-Mbongo,Mobayi-Mbongo Territory, Nord-Ubangi Province in Democratic Republic of the Congo as observed from SPOT 7 imagery acquired on 16 November 2019. UNITAR-UNOSAT has identified about 60 buildings/houses likely surrounded by waters. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to UNITAR -UNOSAT.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/flood-waters-over-mobayi-mbongo-nord-ubangi-province-democratic-republic-of-the-congo]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts interpreted SPOT 7 satellite imagery from 16 November 2019 by comparing pre- and post-flood images to detect changes in water extent along the Ubangui River. Flooded areas were digitized as polygons with area measurements, and building structures within or adjacent to flood waters were identified and counted. This preliminary rapid assessment was conducted without field validation.

sources.name: UN Operational Satellite Applications Programme (UNOSAT)
sources.description: SPOT 7 satellite imagery acquired 16 November 2019 used to detect and delineate flood water extent and identify affected buildings through visual interpretation and multi-temporal image comparison
